condition: Severe pre-eclampsia / HELLP presenting with epigastric pain
permutationLabel: Pregnant, 35 weeks, HELLP mimicking biliary pain
summary: 29-year-old primigravida at 35 weeks with a day of epigastric/RUQ pain, vomiting, headache and flashing lights; BP 172/114, proteinuria 3+, ALT 212, platelets 88. Biliary mimic; NICE NG133: same-day obstetric admission.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Upper abdominal pain and vomiting in pregnancy
inputs.hpi: First pregnancy, 35 weeks. Referred as ?biliary colic: one day of constant pain in the upper abdomen and under the right ribs, vomiting, a frontal headache and flashing lights. Swollen face and hands this week. Missed her last antenatal visit.

exam.abdomen: Tender epigastrium and right upper quadrant, no guarding, gravid uterus consistent with dates, non-tender.
exam.neuro: Brisk reflexes, 3 beats of ankle clonus.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Severe pre-eclampsia with suspected HELLP syndrome
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Severe pre-eclampsia with suspected HELLP (epigastric pain, BP 172/114, proteinuria, ALT 212, platelets 88) - not biliary: same-day obstetric admission, antihypertensive treatment.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: not in top 3 of web.pane: 1. Acute Cholecystitis | 2. Acute Pancreatitis | 3. Peptic Ulcer Disease. PANE has no hypertensive-disorder-of-pregnancy node (obstetric nodes: ectopic pregnancy only).
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Pregnancy branch in the hypertension prompt: BP >=160/110 at >=20 weeks -> suspected severe pre-eclampsia, same-day obstetric admission, labetalol/nifedipine/methyldopa (no ACE inhibitors, ARBs or amlodipine first-line); suppress cholecystectomy/appendicectomy cascades; add pre-eclampsia/HELLP to the differential.

mustExclude.note: Wrong procedure: HELLP mimicking biliary pain.

mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: forbidden management item present in web.clinicalPrompts: "laparoscopic appendicectomy - operative plan ───────────────────────────────────────────── pre-operative: •...".
mustExclude.proposedFix: Gate the appendicectomy cascade on the working diagnosis; negation-aware exam matching ("no guarding").

mustExclude.note: ACE inhibitors/ARBs are contraindicated in pregnancy.
NSAIDs after 20 weeks and with thrombocytopenia/HELLP are contraindicated.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: forbidden management item present in web.clinicalPrompts: "... convert to oral when tolerating po. • paracetamol 1g qds + ibuprofen 400mg tds (regular). • morphine 5mg prn if pain > 5/10. • regular diet as toler...".
mustExclude.proposedFix: Strip NSAIDs from operative templates from 20 weeks of gestation (HPB findings gap 6), and suppress operative templates here altogether.

mustExclude.note: NICE NG133 first-line agents are labetalol, nifedipine or methyldopa.

guideline.name: NICE NG133 - Hypertension in pregnancy: diagnosis and management
guideline.section: Severe hypertension = BP >=160/110 mmHg; pre-eclampsia features include severe headache, visual disturbance, severe pain below the ribs or epigastric pain, vomiting, and HELLP (haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets); severe hypertension or suspected severe pre-eclampsia -> same-day obstetric assessment/admission and antihypertensive treatment
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NG133. London: NICE; 2019 (updated 2023).

rationale: Pregnancy permutation and a biliary mimic: epigastric/RUQ pain is a severe pre-eclampsia feature (HELLP). The surgical engines are expected to reach for gallstones; the blood pressure and pregnancy should redirect.
